title: introduce-delegated-credential-chain-and-async-iterable-wrappers-cross-sdk
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a delegated credential chain and pluggable reauthentication hooks across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; introduces lightweight async iterable wrappers for streaming responses; bumps SDK versions: python v1.12.0, typescript v2.4.0, go v1.6.1. Migration note: credential provider interface gains an optional renew() hook — existing providers continue to work but implementing renew enables automatic proactive refresh.
description:
Motivation: multiple customers and internal teams hit edge cases where a single static credential/provider was insufficient (short-lived tokens, external STS exchanges). This PR introduces a delegated credential chain abstraction plus optional pluggable reauth hooks so SDKs can proactively refresh tokens and fall back to a chain of providers. While adding the chain we also took the opportunity to improve streaming ergonomics by introducing thin async iterable wrappers (TypeScript/Go iterator facade, Python async generator shim) so users have a consistent ergonomic surface across languages.

Scope (single-string): - Add DelegatedCredentialChain (SDK core) with priority/fallback semantics and configuration via environment/constructor. - Add PluggableReauthHook interface (optional) that credential providers can implement to receive renew signals and to perform async exchange. - Implement shims in sdk/python, sdk/typescript, sdk/go to adopt the chain and call renew when token TTL <= threshold. - Introduce AsyncIterable/AsyncGenerator wrappers for streaming APIs that normalize chunk events across runtimes. - Bump package versions and update CHANGELOG entries. - Tests: unit + integration + basic e2e smoke on hosted test cluster.

Checklist: [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-4321). [x] Implement core credential chain and hook interfaces. [x] SDK adaptors implemented for python/ts/go. [x] Add cross-language test harness for simulated short-lived tokens. [x] Update examples and quickstarts. [x] Release notes drafted.

Implementation notes: - Credential chain is configured with a list of providers. The first provider that returns a valid token is used; on failure we iterate providers. Providers can optionally implement renew(ctx) which the SDK will call proactively (TTL-driven) or reactively on 401. - Renew semantics are best-effort and asynchronous; errors bubble to the request path and will trigger fallback policies. - Async iterable wrappers unify error propagation, backpressure signals, and resume semantics; they intentionally keep a minimal surface (Symbol.asyncIterator / AsyncGenerator for TS/Python; channel-like iterator for Go). - To avoid duplication we factored shared logic into the redwood/sdk-core package and added thin language bindings.

Compatibility & migration: - Default behavior is backward compatible: existing providers and code continue to function. - If you want proactive refresh, implement the optional renew() method on your provider or wrap an STS exchange provider included in examples. - Streaming wrappers are additive; existing callback-based streaming APIs remain supported for a deprecation cycle.

Performance & reliability: - Added targeted microbenchmarks: proactive renew latency added ~0.3ms median per request for checked TTL paths (cold path only). Batching and cache hits are unaffected. - Integration tests included a failover scenario: primary provider returns 401 -> chain falls back to swap provider -> request retried once with new token.

Testing: - Unit: python pytest, ts jest, go test. - Integration: ran against staging router with short-lived tokens. - E2E: basic request+stream smoke.
